jobs.title: Computer Vision & Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description:
**What to Expect**

Own the path from line images to a solution Tesla can trust. We collect images on PCBA and TLA lines and developing models that to do this. Your job is to determine what the images can support, prove or kill an approach on our data, and leave us with a solution that works in production, whether that is a model we run, a system we buy, or a clear stop.

You will work with Supplier industrialization engineers, and internal Tesla stakeholders, external solution providers. You will be expected to identify a solution; you will not be handed a labeled dataset or a chosen architecture.

  
**What You'll Do**

* Assess line images for camera, lighting, resolution, and consistency across lines and products, and determine whether defects are visible and separable from normal variation
* Turn the quality problem into a testable vision problem, including which defect is in scope, the acceptable miss rate and false-reject rate, and the cycle time the result must meet
* Build the minimum dataset and labeling approach for rare defects, weak labels, and a large volume of good images
* Select classification, detection, segmentation, or anomaly detection based on the data, not a predetermined architecture
* Run a time-boxed proof on our images, comparing a small set of real options, including classical vision, a trained model, and a commercial AOI or vision system
* Recommend build versus buy, including what data, lighting, or camera changes are required before scaling
* Pilot the chosen approach on one line, covering latency, station integration, traceability, and monitoring
* Validate the chosen system on production data, covering holdout images, line trials, golden-sample checks, and other vision-system validation methods as the case requires
* Define the retraining path for product or process changes
* Report negative results with evidence when the images or the line cannot support the decision

  
**What You'll Bring**

* Several years shipping computer vision into a real operation, not only notebooks and benchmarks
* Factory, AOI, electronics, or other industrial inspection experience
* Experience in PCBA and electronic assembly manufacturing, including IPC workmanship and inspection standards
* Hands-on experience in detection, segmentation, classification, or visual anomaly detection, including labeling, class imbalance, domain shift, and threshold setting
* Ability to evaluate a model on escape rate, false rejects, and cycle time, not only accuracy or mAP
* Judgment to recommend a commercial system when it is the better path, and to distinguish a vendor demo from a result on our images
* Ability to work with design engineer, process and quality engineers and turn their defect definitions into a testable problem
* Proficiency in Python and a standard training stack
* Experience deploying a model to a station, edge device, or factory server
* Evidence of stopping an approach because the images or the operation could not support it

#### **Benefits**

Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:

* Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
* Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
* Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution
* Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
* Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* 401(k) with employer match, Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and other financial benefits
* Company paid Basic Life, AD&D
* Short-term and long-term disability insurance (90 day waiting period)
* Employee Assistance Program
* Sick and Vacation time (Flex time for salary positions, Accrued hours for Hourly positions), and Paid Holidays

* Earned Wage Access: Real-time pay access paid daily, subject to eligibility and schedule (applicable for below Sr. Managers levels)

  

#### **Expected Compensation**

$100,000 - $372,000/annual salary + cash and stock awards + benefits

jobs.title: Research Engineer/Scientist - Dexterous Manipulation
jobs.description:
**About Flexion**

At Flexion, we're building the intelligence layer powering the next generation of humanoid robots. Our mission is to accelerate the transition from fragile prototypes to real-world humanoid deployment. We are founded by leading scientists in robot reinforcement learning (ex-Nvidia, ex-ETH Zürich), and backed by leading international VC firms. In just months, we’ve gone from our first line of code to deploying real humanoid capabilities.

**The role**

We are seeking an expert in dexterous manipulation and large-scale modeling to lead the development of our physical foundation models. The goal of this position is to leverage internet-scale egocentric video to build Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models that enable our humanoid robots to interact with the world with human-like fluidity. You bring a deep understanding of how to bridge the gap between observing human actions in video and executing high-DOF (20+) motor control.

As a Research Engineer for Dexterous Manipulation at Flexion, you’ll work in our Zürich office to develop and deploy state-of-the-art learning-based controllers. You will take ownership of the model architecture, integrating egocentric priors with real-time robot policies, to ensure our hardware can manipulate objects reliably and flexibly in unstructured environments.

**Key Responsibilities**

* Scalable Egocentric Pre-training: Architect and implement large-scale pre-training objectives for egocentric video datasets to learn generalizable representations of hand-object interactions and spatial-temporal dynamics.
* VLA Foundation Modeling: Develop and scale multi-modal Foundation Models that unify visual perception and natural language instructions into actionable robotic trajectories.
* Generative Policy Design: Design and optimize generative action heads using Diffusion Models and Flow-matching techniques to capture the multi-modal distribution of complex human movements.
* Humanoid Motion Alignment: Develop novel algorithms to align human-centric video representations with the kinematic constraints of 20+ DoF humanoid systems, ensuring fluid and stable execution.
* Reinforcement Learning & Fine-tuning: Utilize Offline RL and high-fidelity simulation fine-tuning to optimize foundation model performance for high-success-rate physical manipulation.
* Cross-Functional Research: Translate cutting-edge research in scaling laws and world models into production-ready architectures that enhance robot reliability and autonomy.

  
**Requirements**  

* PhD or Master’s degree in Robotics, Machine Learning, or a closely related field, with a strong focus on data-driven manipulation, egocentric vision, or foundation models.
* Experience with Humanoid or Dexterous Manipulation, including a deep understanding of contact-rich physics.
* Excellent knowledge of Python, PyTorch, and the distributed training of large-scale neural networks (FSDP, NCCL).
* Proven expertise in Diffusion Models, Flow Matching, and Transformers.
* Hands-on experience deploying learning-based controllers on real robot hardware.
* Experience with Reinforcement Learning and simulation environments (e.g., IsaacLab, MuJoCo)

  
**Benefits**  

* + Competitive compensation
  + Enhanced pension plan
  + Enhanced holiday & paid leave perks
  + Relocation & permit sponsorship
  + Central Zürich office with top-tier robotics testing facilities and infrastructure
  + Joining Europe's leading robotics team & exposure to never-done-before research
  + Energetic, collaborative culture with a bias for action and regular community events

**About Pocket**

*At Pocket, we’re building the future of human memory.*

Some of the most valuable information in our lives disappears when a conversation ends: an idea, a decision, a detail we wish we could remember. Pocket helps us hold onto it.

We’ve built an AI-powered device that captures real-world conversations and turns them into searchable transcripts, summaries and next steps. Backed by Accel and Y Combinator (W26), we’ve already sold 500,000 devices.

Our ambition goes beyond recording. We believe the things you learn, discuss and experience can become useful context for the AI tools you already use, and for products that don’t exist yet.

Real conversations are messy. People interrupt, rooms are noisy, speakers sound similar and a missed detail can change the meaning of a summary.

You’ll improve the voice systems that make Pocket useful in those conditions. The work connects applied research to production: define the problem, build an evaluation, test an approach and ship what works. You’ll partner with product and design so technical progress becomes something customers can notice.

* Improvements to diarization, voice activity detection, noise robustness, transcription, speaker identification and post-processing.
* Voice-powered capabilities such as better summaries, action extraction, memory and personalization.
* Research loops with explicit metrics, representative evaluation sets and repeatable comparisons.
* Moving promising models and algorithms from prototypes into reliable product features.
* Streaming performance, latency, fallbacks and behavior when systems cannot produce a confident answer.

**What We’re Looking For**

* 6–10+ years shipping production systems with strong technical ownership.
* Applied ML or research-engineering experience, including turning prototypes into dependable software.
* A working understanding of audio and voice fundamentals, modern models and evaluation workflows.
* Care for performance, reliability and the failure cases that a demo can hide.
* The ability to work with product and design and explain technical tradeoffs clearly.

**Bonus Points**

Streaming audio and real-time systems; LLM post-processing and structured extraction; or tools for labeling, dataset curation and quality assurance. Signal-processing fundamentals are useful too.

**What Success Looks Like**

Voice quality improves on meaningful evaluations and in everyday use. An offline and online evaluation system catches regressions. New capabilities reach customers with predictable latency and reliable behavior.

**Why Join Pocket?**

You’ll work on voice captured by a real consumer device, with a direct path from an experiment to a shipped feature. The job gives you room to investigate hard problems without losing the connection to the person relying on the result.

Compensation Range: $200K - $300K

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.

We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

**The role**

Our operators control robots across countries and oceans. You'll own the link between them: getting multiple camera streams to the operator and commands back to the robot with as little delay and jitter as physics allows, and building the interface operators use all day. Because every byte you stream is also training data, you'll own recording it on-site and getting it reliably off-site too.

**What you'll do**

* Build the real-time transport between robot sites and operator stations: low-latency video (multiple cameras, possibly depth), robot state, and control commands over the public internet.
* Own the end-to-end latency budget. Instrument glass-to-glass and command-to-motion latency, find where every millisecond goes, and cut it: encoding settings, transport choice, routing, jitter buffers, relay placement.
* Make the link robust: NAT traversal, congestion and packet loss, bandwidth adaptation, reconnection, and clear signals to the operator and robot when quality degrades.
* Design and build the operator interface: camera layouts, robot state and health, task instructions, latency and connection indicators, and fast workflows for starting, labeling, and ending episodes.
* Build operator-facing tooling: queueing operators to robots across sites, session handoff, and basic fleet visibility.
* Own on-site recording: capture synchronized streams and metadata into a well-defined episode format, buffer locally, and upload reliably over constrained site networks.
* Set up the infrastructure for data storage and access of robot teleop episodes.

**What we're looking for**

* 3+ years building production level real-time networked systems: video streaming, video conferencing, cloud gaming, remote desktop, live broadcast, or similar.
* Hands-on experience with low-latency media transport (e.g., WebRTC, RTP/SRTP, QUIC/UDP-based protocols) and video encoding trade-offs.

* Comfortable building a polished interface yourself, web or native, with good product instincts for people who use a tool eight hours a day.
* Strong in at least one of TypeScript, Go, Rust, C++, or Python; comfortable across client, server, and edge devices.

new_jobs.description:
**What to Expect**

Own the path from line images to a solution Tesla can trust. We collect images on PCBA and TLA lines and developing models that to do this. Your job is to determine what the images can support, prove or kill an approach on our data, and leave us with a solution that works in production, whether that is a model we run, a system we buy, or a clear stop.

You will work with Supplier industrialization engineers, and internal Tesla stakeholders, external solution providers. You will be expected to identify a solution; you will not be handed a labeled dataset or a chosen architecture.

  
**What You'll Do**

* Assess line images for camera, lighting, resolution, and consistency across lines and products, and determine whether defects are visible and separable from normal variation
* Turn the quality problem into a testable vision problem, including which defect is in scope, the acceptable miss rate and false-reject rate, and the cycle time the result must meet
* Build the minimum dataset and labeling approach for rare defects, weak labels, and a large volume of good images
* Select classification, detection, segmentation, or anomaly detection based on the data, not a predetermined architecture
* Run a time-boxed proof on our images, comparing a small set of real options, including classical vision, a trained model, and a commercial AOI or vision system
* Recommend build versus buy, including what data, lighting, or camera changes are required before scaling
* Pilot the chosen approach on one line, covering latency, station integration, traceability, and monitoring
* Validate the chosen system on production data, covering holdout images, line trials, golden-sample checks, and other vision-system validation methods as the case requires
* Define the retraining path for product or process changes
* Report negative results with evidence when the images or the line cannot support the decision

  
**What You'll Bring**

* Several years shipping computer vision into a real operation, not only notebooks and benchmarks
* Factory, AOI, electronics, or other industrial inspection experience
* Experience in PCBA and electronic assembly manufacturing, including IPC workmanship and inspection standards
* Hands-on experience in detection, segmentation, classification, or visual anomaly detection, including labeling, class imbalance, domain shift, and threshold setting
* Ability to evaluate a model on escape rate, false rejects, and cycle time, not only accuracy or mAP
* Judgment to recommend a commercial system when it is the better path, and to distinguish a vendor demo from a result on our images
* Ability to work with design engineer, process and quality engineers and turn their defect definitions into a testable problem
* Proficiency in Python and a standard training stack
* Experience deploying a model to a station, edge device, or factory server
* Evidence of stopping an approach because the images or the operation could not support it

### **About Mecka AI**

Mecka AI is building the data infrastructure layer for robotics and embodied AI.  
We design and operate global systems for data capture, data labeling, and hardware-enabled workflows used by leading AI labs and robotics companies to train and validate humanoid and embodied AI systems.  
We work closely with frontier robotics teams to bridge real-world data, simulation, learning-based systems, and deployed hardware.

**The role**

Our operators control robots across countries and oceans. You'll own the link between them: getting multiple camera streams to the operator and commands back to the robot with as little delay and jitter as physics allows, and building the interface operators use all day. Because every byte you stream is also training data, you'll own recording it on-site and getting it reliably off-site too.

**What you'll do**

* Build the real-time transport between robot sites and operator stations: low-latency video (multiple cameras, possibly depth), robot state, and control commands over the public internet.
* Own the end-to-end latency budget. Instrument glass-to-glass and command-to-motion latency, find where every millisecond goes, and cut it: encoding settings, transport choice, routing, jitter buffers, relay placement.
* Make the link robust: NAT traversal, congestion and packet loss, bandwidth adaptation, reconnection, and clear signals to the operator and robot when quality degrades.
* Design and build the operator interface: camera layouts, robot state and health, task instructions, latency and connection indicators, and fast workflows for starting, labeling, and ending episodes.
* Build operator-facing tooling: queueing operators to robots across sites, session handoff, and basic fleet visibility.
* Own on-site recording: capture synchronized streams and metadata into a well-defined episode format, buffer locally, and upload reliably over constrained site networks.
* Set up the infrastructure for data storage and access of robot teleop episodes.

**What we're looking for**

* 3+ years building production level real-time networked systems: video streaming, video conferencing, cloud gaming, remote desktop, live broadcast, or similar.
* Hands-on experience with low-latency media transport (e.g., WebRTC, RTP/SRTP, QUIC/UDP-based protocols) and video encoding trade-offs.

* Comfortable building a polished interface yourself, web or native, with good product instincts for people who use a tool eight hours a day.
